issues.issue: The no-consent representation is qualified by "except as contemplated herein or therein," an open-ended carve-out that swallows the representation's boundary.

The representation excepts "Proceedings of general applicability and those related to market transitions" and also "immaterial claims brought ... in the ordinary course of business," leaving the carve-outs' reach uncertain.

The representation is stacked with qualifiers — "only to the best knowledge," "assuming compliance ... by other parties to a Third Party Agreement," and "complied in all respects" subject to a Material Adverse Effect carve-out — so its actual content is genuinely contestable.

The knowledge qualifier here interacts with Section 8.02, which directs that Damages be measured "without regard to any limitation or qualification as to materiality ... knowledge or similar language" in the representation.
"[B]est knowledge after commercially reasonable investigation" including "all facts which it knew or should have known" is a constructive-knowledge standard with no defined scope of investigation.
Clearwire Parent is made the subject of a representation in an Article given by Clearwire alone, although Clearwire Parent is not a Party under the preamble.
The representation is given by "[e]ach of Clearwire Parent and Clearwire," yet only Clearwire is a Party under the preamble and only Clearwire executes the Agreement.

"[H]as complied in all respects" is immediately qualified "other than where noncompliance would not ... have a Clearwire Material Adverse Effect," leaving the standard of compliance internally at odds.

"[C]ommercially reasonable efforts" is undefined and the clause imposes on each Party efforts to obtain consents "required to be obtained by Clearwire and the Licensee," so which Party bears which consent is unclear.
The notice duty is triggered only by matters "which Licensee determines is reasonably likely to constitute a breach," a subjective trigger the obligated party controls.

The covenant is hedged by "[e]xcept as such qualifications may be affected by this Agreement" and by a proviso excusing loss of an FCC Qualification caused "in whole or in part" by Clearwire, so it is uncertain when a breach can occur at all.

The opening limit that this Section "appl[ies] only to spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA" is difficult to reconcile with the same Section's reference to Clearwire's obligation to meet the substantial service requirement on Licensee's licensed spectrum.

The Section is expressed to apply "only to spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA," yet its final sentence permits Licensee to assign "this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder" to affiliates without consent — a scope mismatch within the provision.
The free affiliate assignment right sits against Section 10.09's reference to "permitted assigns" and against the consent machinery in the earlier sentences of this same Section.

The Parties "agree not to express any contrary view to regulatory agencies or the general public" about FCC compliance, an obligation of uncertain reach against the duty in the first sentence to comply with FCC rules at all times.

Clearwire must pay "all fees and taxes (now existing or hereafter arising) imposed on Licensee as a result of the licensing, regulation or use of Licensee's EBS Spectrum by Clearwire or Licensee," and whether "EBS Spectrum" reaches spectrum not under an IUA and taxes flowing from Licensee's own use is genuinely open.
This broad tax undertaking overlaps and may conflict with Section 10.01, which allocates only sales, use and similar transfer taxes "in connection with the Transactions" to Clearwire.

A covenant "to act in a cooperative manner to preserve the intent of the relationships" and to use "commercially reasonable best efforts to maintain that mutual advantage in accordance with the initial intent of the Parties" states no ascertainable obligation.

Clause (iii) indemnifies for matters "otherwise related to the activities of Clearwire, any of its Affiliates or any of its sublicensees or resellers including, without limitation, damage to health," a catch-all of indeterminate reach against the specific operation-of-equipment and provision-of-service items.

"Damages" is defined to include "statutory or regulatory compliance requirements" and matters "of every kind and description, contingent or otherwise," with no exclusion of consequential loss, so its outer limit is contestable.

The Deductible is stated to apply to liability "under Section 8.01(a)(i) or Section 8.01(b)(i)" — the representation-and-warranty limbs — yet the operative words also speak of "the breach of any covenant," which is indemnified under the (ii) limbs that are not subject to the Deductible.
As drafted the covenant reference here cannot be squared with Sections 8.01(a)(ii) and 8.01(b)(ii), which impose covenant indemnities without any threshold.

The clause preserves the indemnity despite late notice "except to the extent that the indemnifying Party can demonstrate actual loss and prejudice," qualifying the "reasonably and promptly" notice requirement of Section 8.04(a) in a way whose effect must be construed.

Clause (3) makes the Term end when Licensee returns the unused Prepaid Royalties, while Section 2.02 makes that refund due within five days after the Term expires — the two provisions are circular and cannot both be given literal effect; the extension right here also conflicts with Section 2.02's unlimited extension right.
The Term sentence ends with the unexplained qualifier "except as it pertains to Puerto Rico," which identifies no rule for how long the Term runs for Puerto Rico spectrum.

The list of termination events is mis-lettered ("(i)" followed by "(1)" then "(iii)"), and clauses (ii) and (iii) give the two Parties materially different cure periods for the same defined Event of Default.

The direction that on termination "for any cause" the Prepaid Royalties Balance be refunded "as provided in Section 2.02" runs into Section 1.01(b)'s characterisation of part of that payment as consideration for the Option and ROFR.

An "Event of Default" requires failure to perform "a material obligation" in circumstances "where such failure results in the inability of the other party to exercise its full rights," a compound and undefined threshold.
"Loss" is defined only "in the applicable IUA," a document not set out in this instrument, so the trigger for the cooperation duty cannot be read off this Agreement.

Survival of obligations "that by their nature would continue beyond expiration or termination" is an open standard, and the Option/ROFR carve-out extends to events that "would have occurred, if Licensee complied in full."
Indefinite survival of Options and rights of first refusal is hard to reconcile with Section 1.02(d)'s rule that "[a]ny outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term."
The obligation runs to the "Licensee(s) Indemnified Parties," a term defined in Section 8.01(b) as the "Licensee Indemnified Parties," and overlaps Section 7.06's broader fee-and-tax undertaking.

The statement that "[a]ll agreements and covenants contained herein shall survive indefinitely" sits against Section 9.03, which limits survival to obligations that "by their nature would continue beyond expiration or termination."
The entire-agreement statement must be squared with the Agreement's dependence on the IUAs, Collateral Documents and Exhibit I definitions referred to in Sections 1.01(a), 1.03 and the preamble.

Notice is "deemed given when delivered personally or by overnight courier, or mailed by certified mail," so for certified mail the deeming event is dispatch rather than receipt despite the return-receipt requirement; the Kirkland, Washington addressee is also given a 415 area-code facsimile number.
"[T]o the extent possible, allow the other Party reasonable time to comment" sets an unmeasurable qualification on the publicity exception.

The one-sentence severability clause says only that "the balance of this Agreement shall remain in effect," with no reformation or essential-term qualification, so its effect on a failed core term such as the Option pricing would have to be construed.
"[P]ermitted assigns" presupposes an assignment-restriction provision, but the Agreement contains no general anti-assignment clause other than the FCC-license-specific Section 7.04.

The clause both stipulates that "monetary damages alone will not be adequate" and preserves "money damages" as a cumulative remedy, an internal tension a court would have to reconcile before ordering specific performance.
The cumulative-remedies and specific-performance rights sit against Section 10.11, which makes the Dispute Resolution Procedures the Parties' "sole means" of resolving disputes.

The provision states the Dispute Resolution Procedures are the Parties' "sole means" but the sentence is cut off, so the scope of disputes covered and whether resort to court is barred cannot be determined from the words.

A "sole means" dispute procedure cannot easily be squared with Section 10.10's guarantee of specific performance and cumulative remedies "at law or in equity," nor with the ad hoc arbitration references in Sections 1.04 and 3.03(b).
